a hospital; and
a government department; and
a government agency; and
a municipal council; and
a public sector body; and
a sporting group; and
a youth organisation; and

a charity or benevolent
organisation; or

an organisation that, in accordance
with an agreement or arrangement
with an organisation referred to in
paragraph (a), is required or permitted
to engage in activities associated with
the care, supervision or authority over
children exercised by the organisation
referred to in paragraph (a);
sexual offence means—

an offence against a provision of
Subdivision (8A), this Subdivision
(other than this section), (8C), (8D),
, (8F) or (8FA); or

an attempt to commit an
offence covered by paragraph (a)
(other than section 49K); or

an assault with intent to commit an
offence covered by paragraph (a).

nodes.heading: Abduction or detention of a child under the age of 16 for a sexual purpose

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A—

takes away or detains another
person (B); or

causes B to be taken away or detained
by another person; and
B is a child under the age of 16 years; and

the person who has lawful charge of B (C)
does not consent to B being taken away or
detained; and
A knows that—

B is a child under the age of 16 years;
or

B is probably a child under the age
of 16 years; and
A knows that—

C does not consent to B being taken
away or detained; or

C probably does not consent to B being
taken away or detained; and

A intends B will take part in a sexual act
with A or another person or both; and

B taking part in the sexual act would involve
the commission by A, or the other person, or
both, of an offence against section 38(1),
39(1), 40(1), 41(1) or a provision of this
Subdivision (other than this section).

A person who commits an offence against
subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment
(10 years maximum).
See section 35C for the meaning of taking part in a sexual act.

nodes.heading: Causing or allowing a sexual performance involving a child

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—

A intentionally causes or allows another
person (B) to take part in a sexual
performance; and

the sexual performance occurs in
circumstances that involve any person
receiving payment, reward or other benefit
(whether before or after the performance)
in respect of the performance; and
B is a child under the age of 18 years.

A person who commits an offence against
subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment
(10 years maximum).

In this section—
sexual performance means a live performance
(whether in person or by an electronic
communication within the meaning of
the Electronic Transactions (Victoria)
Act 2000) that is, or could reasonably be
considered to be, for the sexual arousal or
sexual gratification of any person.
A defence applies to this offence—see section 49X.

A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that the sexual
performance did not occur in circumstances that involved
payment, reward or other benefit to any person is not a
defence to this offence—see section 49ZC.

nodes.heading: Inviting or offering a sexual performance involving a child

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally—

invites another person (B) to take part
in a sexual performance; or

offers to a third person that B will take
part in a sexual performance; and

the invitation or offer involves any person
receiving payment, reward or other benefit
(whether before or after the performance) in
respect of the performance; and
B is a child under the age of 18 years.

A person who commits an offence against
subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment
(10 years maximum).

In this section—
sexual performance means a live performance
(whether in person or by an electronic
communication within the meaning of
the Electronic Transactions (Victoria)
Act 2000) that is, or could reasonably be
considered to be, for the sexual arousal or
sexual gratification of any person.
A defence applies to this offence—see section 49X.

A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that the
invitation or offer did not involve payment, reward or other
benefit to any person is not a defence to this offence—see
section 49ZC.

nodes.heading: Facilitating a sexual offence against a child

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—

A engages in conduct that aids, facilitates or
contributes in any way to another person (B)
engaging in sexual conduct (whether or not
in Victoria) in relation to a child; and

A engages in the conduct with the intention
of obtaining a benefit for A or another
person (C); and
A—

intends that the conduct will aid,
facilitate or contribute in any way to B
engaging in sexual conduct in relation
to a child; or

knows that the conduct will, or
probably will, aid, facilitate or
contribute in any way to B engaging in
sexual conduct in relation to a child;
and

B's engaging in sexual conduct in relation to
a child—

constitutes an offence against
section 38(1), 39(1), 40(1), 41(1)
or a provision of this Subdivision
(other than this section); or

constitutes an offence against
a provision of Division 272 of
Chapter 8 of the Criminal Code
of the Commonwealth; or

takes place outside Victoria but
would, if the conduct occurred
in Victoria, constitute an offence
against a provision covered by
subparagraph (i) whether or not it
constitutes an offence in the place
in which it takes place.

A person who commits an offence against
subsection (1) is liable to level 3 imprisonment
(20 years maximum).

For the purposes of subsection (1), conduct
that aids, facilitates or contributes in any way
to another person engaging in sexual conduct
in relation to a child includes—
making travel arrangements; and

causing or allowing a child to enter or
remain on premises which A owns,
occupies, manages or assists in managing.

A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that B's engaging in
sexual conduct in relation to a child did not constitute an offence
or, if the conduct takes place outside Victoria, would not constitute
an offence, is not a defence to this offence—see section 49ZC.

nodes.heading: Exception to sexual penetration offences—medical or hygienic purposes
nodes.text:
A does not commit an offence against
section 49A(1), 49B(1) or 49C(1) if A's conduct
occurs in the course of a procedure carried out
in good faith for medical or hygienic purposes.

The reference to A in this section is a reference to the same
A referred to in sections 49A, 49B and 49C.

nodes.heading: Exceptions to offences against children under 16— similarity in age

nodes.text:
A does not commit an offence against
section 49D(1) or 49F(1) if, at the time at
which the offence is alleged to have been
committed—
A is not more than 2 years older than B; and
B is 12 years of age or more.

A does not commit an offence against
section 49H(1) if, at the time at which the
offence is alleged to have been committed—
A is not more than 2 years older than C; and
C is 12 years of age or more.

References to A, B and C in this section are references to the same
A, B and C referred to in sections 49D, 49F and 49H.

nodes.heading: Defence to offence against a child under 16— similarity in age
nodes.text:
It is a defence to a charge for an offence against
section 49B(1) if, at the time of the conduct
constituting the offence—

A was not more than 2 years older than B;
and
B was 12 years of age or more; and
B consented to the sexual penetration.

References to A and B in this section are references to the same
A and B referred to in section 49B.

nodes.heading: Defences to offences against children under 16— reasonable belief as to age

nodes.text:
It is a defence to a charge for an offence against
section 49B(1), 49D(1) or 49F(1) if, at the time of
the conduct constituting the offence—
B was 12 years of age or more; and

A reasonably believed that B was 16 years of
age or more.

It is a defence to a charge for an offence against
section 49H(1) if, at the time of the conduct
constituting the offence—
C was 12 years of age or more; and

A reasonably believed that C was 16 years of
age or more.

It is a defence to a charge for an offence against
section 49K(1) if, at the time of the conduct
constituting the offence, A reasonably believed
that B was 16 years of age or more.

A bears the burden of proving (on the balance of
probabilities) the matter referred to in subsection

References to A, B and C in this section are references to the
same A, B and C referred to in sections 49B, 49D, 49F, 49H
and 49K.
Whether or not A reasonably believed that B or C was

years of age or more depends on the circumstances.
The circumstances include any steps that A took to find out
B or C's age.

An evidential burden applies to the matters referred to in
subsections (1)(a) and (2)(a).

nodes.heading: Defences to offences against children aged 16 or 17 or under 18—reasonable belief as to age

nodes.text:
It is a defence to a charge for an offence against
section 49C(1), 49E(1), 49G(1) or 49L(1) if, at
the time of the conduct constituting the offence,
A reasonably believed that B was 18 years of age
or more.

It is a defence to a charge for an offence against
section 49I(1) if, at the time of the conduct
constituting the offence, A reasonably believed
that C was 18 years of age or more.

It is a defence to a charge for an offence against
section 49Q(1) or 49R(1) if, at the time of the
conduct constituting the offence—
B was 12 years of age or more; and

A reasonably believed that B was 18 years of
age or more.

A bears the burden of proving (on the balance of
probabilities) the matter referred to in subsection

References to A, B and C in this section are references to the
same A, B and C referred to in sections 49C, 49E, 49G, 49I,
49L, 49Q and 49R.
Whether or not A reasonably believed that B or C was

years of age or more depends on the circumstances.
The circumstances include any steps that A took to find
out B or C's age.

An evidential burden applies to the matter referred to in
subsection (3)(a).

nodes.heading: Exceptions to offences against children aged 16 or 17—marriage or domestic partnership

nodes.text:
A does not commit an offence against
section 49C(1), 49E(1), 49G(1) or 49L(1)
if, at the time at which the offence is alleged
to have been committed—

A and B are married to each other and the
marriage is recognised as valid under the
Marriage Act 1961 of the Commonwealth; or
A—

is not more than 5 years older than B;
and

is B's domestic partner and the
domestic partnership commenced
before B came under A's care,
supervision or authority.

A does not commit an offence against
section 49I(1) if, at the time at which the
offence is alleged to have been committed—

A and C are married to each other and the
marriage is recognised as valid under the
Marriage Act 1961 of the Commonwealth; or
A—

is not more than 5 years older than C;
and

is C's domestic partner and the
domestic partnership commenced
before C came under A's care,
supervision or authority.

References to A, B and C in this section are references to the same
A, B and C referred to in sections 49C, 49E, 49G, 49I and 49L.

nodes.heading: Defences to offences against children aged 16 or 17—reasonable belief as to marriage or domestic partnership

nodes.text:
It is a defence to a charge for an offence against
section 49C(1), 49E(1), 49G(1) or 49L(1) if, at the
time of the conduct constituting the offence—

A reasonably believed that A and B were
married to each other and that the marriage
was recognised as valid under the Marriage
Act 1961 of the Commonwealth; or
A—

was not more than 5 years older than B;
and

reasonably believed that A was B's
domestic partner and that the domestic
partnership commenced before B came
under A's care, supervision or authority.

It is a defence to a charge for an offence against
section 49I(1) if, at the time of the conduct
constituting the offence—

A reasonably believed that A and C were
married to each other and that the marriage
was recognised as valid under the Marriage
Act 1961 of the Commonwealth; or
A—

was not more than 5 years older than C;
and

reasonably believed that A was C's
domestic partner and that the domestic
partnership commenced before C came
under A's care, supervision or authority.

A bears the burden of proving (on the balance of
probabilities) the matter referred to in subsection
(a) or (b)(ii) or (2)(a) or (b)(ii).

References to A, B and C in this section are references to the
same A, B and C referred to in sections 49C, 49E, 49G, 49I
and 49L.

An evidential burden applies to the matters referred to in
subsections (1)(b)(i) and (2)(b)(i).

nodes.heading: Defences to offences against children aged 16 or 17—reasonable belief as to care, supervision or authority

nodes.text:
It is a defence to a charge for an offence against
section 49C(1), 49E(1), 49G(1) or 49L(1) if, at
the time of the conduct constituting the offence,
A reasonably believed that B was not under A's
care, supervision or authority.

It is a defence to a charge for an offence against
section 49I(1) if, at the time of the conduct
constituting the offence, A reasonably believed
that C was not under A's care, supervision or
authority.

A bears the burden of proving (on the balance of
probabilities) the matter referred to in subsection

References to A, B and C in this section are references to the same
A, B and C referred to in sections 49C, 49E, 49G, 49I and 49L.

nodes.heading: Exception to loitering offence
nodes.text:
A does not commit an offence against
section 49N(1) if A has a reasonable excuse
for loitering at or near a place referred to in
section 49N(1)(c).

The reference to A in this section is a reference to the same
A referred to in section 49N.

nodes.heading: No defence of mistaken but honest and reasonable belief of certain matters
nodes.text:
It is not a defence to a charge that, at the time of
the conduct constituting the offence, A was under
a mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that—

for an offence against section 49A(1)—
B was 12 years of age or more; or

for an offence against section 49D(1)
or 49E(1)—the touching was not—
sexual; or

contrary to community standards of
acceptable conduct; or

for an offence against section 49F(1)
or 49G(1)—
the activity was not sexual; or

engaging in the activity in the presence
of B was not contrary to community
standards of acceptable conduct; or

for an offence against section 49H(1)
or 49I(1)—
the activity was not sexual; or

A's causing or allowing C to be present
when B engages in the activity was not
contrary to community standards of
acceptable conduct; or

for an offence against section 49K(1)
or 49L(1)—the activity was not sexual; or

for an offence against section 49Q(1)—
the sexual performance did not occur in
circumstances that involved payment,
reward or other benefit to any person in
respect of the performance; or

for an offence against section 49R(1)—
the invitation or offer did not involve
payment, reward or other benefit to any
person in respect of the performance; or

for an offence against section 49S(1)—
B's engaging in sexual conduct in relation
to a child did not constitute an offence or,
if the conduct takes place outside Victoria,
would not constitute an offence.

References to A, B and C in this section are references to the same
A, B and C referred to in sections 49A, 49D, 49E, 49F, 49G, 49H,
49I, 49K, 49L, 49Q, 49R and 49S.

history.raw: Pt 1 Div. 1 Subdiv. (8C) (Heading and ss 52, 53) inserted by No. 9509 s. 5, amended2, substituted as Pt 1 Div. 1 Subdiv. (8C) (Heading and ss 50A–50K) by No. 47/2016 s. 16.

nodes.heading: Definitions
nodes.text: In this Subdivision—

nodes.heading: child
nodes.text: , in relation to a person, means—
the person's child by birth; or
the person's genetic child; or

the person's child by operation of the
Adoption Act 1984; or

the person's child by operation of the
Status of Children Act 1974;

nodes.heading: half-sibling
lineal ancestor
nodes.text:
, in relation to a person, means a
lineal ancestor of the person's parent;

nodes.heading: lineal descendant
nodes.text:
, in relation to a person, means a
lineal descendant of the person's child;

nodes.heading: parent
nodes.text: , in relation to a person, means—
the person's birth parent; or
the person's genetic parent; or

the person's parent by operation of the
Adoption Act 1984; or

the person's parent by operation of the
Status of Children Act 1974;

nodes.heading: sibling
nodes.text:
, in relation to a person, means a person
who has the same parents as the person;

nodes.heading: step-parent
nodes.text:
, in relation to a person, means the
spouse or domestic partner of the person's
parent, being a person who is not the
person's parent.

nodes.heading: Rebuttable presumption as to family relationship
nodes.text:
In a proceeding for an offence against a provision
of this Subdivision, there is a rebuttable
presumption that—

A knows that A is related to B in the way
alleged; and

people who are reputed to be related to each
other in a particular way are in fact related in
that way.

nodes.heading: Sexual penetration of a child or lineal descendant

history.raw: Note 4 to s. 50C inserted by No. 65/2016 s. 24(3), substituted by No. 34/2017 s. 33(2).
Note 5 to s. 50C inserted by No. 34/2017 s. 33(2).

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally—

sexually penetrates another person (B);
or

causes or allows B to sexually penetrate
A; and
B is A's child or lineal descendant; and

A knows that B is A's child or lineal
descendant.

A person who commits an offence against
subsection (1) is liable to level 2 imprisonment
(25 years maximum).

The standard sentence for an offence against
subsection (1) is 10 years if B is, at the time
of the offence, under the age of 18 years.
An exception applies to this offence—see section 50G.
A defence applies to this offence—see section 50H.
B's consent is not a defence to this offence—see section 50K.

See sections 5A and 5B of the Sentencing Act 1991 as to
standard sentences.

An offence against subsection (1) is a category 1 offence
under the Sentencing Act 1991 if B is, at the time of the
offence, under the age of 18 years. See section 5(2G) of
that Act for the requirement to impose a custodial order
for this offence.

history.raw: Note 4 to s. 50D inserted by No. 65/2016 s. 24(4), substituted by No. 34/2017 s. 34(2).
Note 5 to s. 50D inserted by No. 34/2017 s. 34(2).

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally—

sexually penetrates another person (B);
or

causes or allows B to sexually penetrate
A; and

B is a child or lineal descendant of A's
spouse or domestic partner; and

A knows that B is a child or lineal
descendant of A's spouse or domestic
partner.

A person who commits an offence against
subsection (1) is liable to level 2 imprisonment
(25 years maximum).

The standard sentence for an offence against
subsection (1) is 10 years if B is, at the time
of the offence, under the age of 18 years.
Exceptions apply to this offence—see sections 50G and 50I.
A defence applies to this offence—see section 50H.
B's consent is not a defence to this offence—see section 50K.

See sections 5A and 5B of the Sentencing Act 1991 as to
standard sentences.

An offence against subsection (1) is a category 1 offence
under the Sentencing Act 1991 if B is, at the time of the
offence, under the age of 18 years. See section 5(2G) of
that Act for the requirement to impose a custodial order for
this offence.

nodes.heading: Sexual penetration of a parent, lineal ancestor or step-parent

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally—

sexually penetrates another person (B);
or

causes or allows B to sexually penetrate
A; and
A is 18 years of age or more; and

B is A's parent, lineal ancestor or
step-parent; and

A knows that B is A's parent, lineal ancestor
or step-parent.

A person who commits an offence against
subsection (1) is liable to level 6 imprisonment
(5 years maximum).
Exceptions apply to this offence—see sections 50G and 50J.
A defence applies to this offence—see section 50H.
B's consent is not a defence to this offence—see section 50K.

nodes.heading: Sexual penetration of a sibling or half-sibling

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally—

sexually penetrates another person (B);
or

causes or allows B to sexually penetrate
A; and
B is A's sibling or half-sibling; and
A knows that B is A's sibling or half-sibling.

A person who commits an offence against
subsection (1) is liable to level 6 imprisonment
(5 years maximum).
An exception applies to this offence—see section 50G.
A defence applies to this offence—see section 50H.
B's consent is not a defence to this offence—see section 50K.

nodes.heading: Exception—medical or hygienic purposes
nodes.text:
A does not commit an offence against a provision
of this Subdivision if A's conduct occurs in the
course of a procedure carried out in good faith for
medical or hygienic purposes.

The reference to A in this section is a reference to the same A
referred to in the offence provisions in this Subdivision.

nodes.heading: Defence—accused did not consent
nodes.text:
It is a defence to a charge for an offence against a
provision of this Subdivision if A did not consent
to the conduct constituting the offence.

history.raw: Note 2 to s. 50H amended by No. 38/2022 s. 12.

nodes.text:
The reference to A in this section is a reference to the same
A referred to in the offence provisions in this Subdivision.

A person may intentionally engage in conduct but not consent
to it—see section 36AA. For example, B threatens to hurt A
if A does not allow B to sexually penetrate A. A intentionally
allows B to sexually penetrate A because A is afraid of harm.
A did not consent to the conduct constituting the offence.

nodes.heading: Exception to offences against section 50D
nodes.text:
A does not commit an offence against
section 50D(1) if, at the time at which the
offence is alleged to have been committed—
B is 18 years of age or more; and

A has not engaged in sexual activity with
B when B was under 18 years of age; and

B has not at any time been under A's care,
supervision or authority.

References to A and B in this section are references to the same
A and B referred to in section 50D.

A does not commit an offence against
section 50E(1) if, at the time at which the
offence is alleged to have been committed—
B is A's step-parent; and

A has not at any time been under B's care,
supervision or authority.

A does not commit an offence against
section 50E(1) if B engaged in sexual activity
with A when A was under 18 years of age.

References to A and B in this section are references to the same
A and B referred to in section 50E.

nodes.heading: Consent not a defence
nodes.text:
It is not a defence to a charge for an offence
against a provision of this Subdivision that B
consented to the conduct constituting the offence.

The reference to B in this section is a reference to the same
B referred to in the offence provisions in this Subdivision.
