nodes.heading: Fraudulently inducing persons to invest
nodes.text: Fraudulently inducing persons to invest

nodes.heading: Fraudulently inducing persons to invest money

nodes.text:
Any person who, by any statement promise or
forecast which he knows to be misleading false or
deceptive or by any dishonest concealment of
material facts or by the reckless making of any
statement promise or forecast which is misleading
false or deceptive, induces or attempts to induce
another person—
shall be guilty of an indictable offence and liable
to level 4 imprisonment (15 years maximum).
to enter into or offer to enter into—

any agreement for or with a view to
acquiring disposing of subscribing in or
underwriting securities or lending or
depositing money to or with any
corporation; or

any agreement the purpose or pretended
purpose of which is to secure a profit to
any of the parties from the yield of
securities or by reference to
fluctuations in the value of securities;
or

to acquire or offer to acquire any right or
interest under any arrangement the purpose
or effect or pretended purpose or effect of
which is to provide facilities for the
participation by persons in profits or income
alleged to arise or to be likely to arise from
the acquisition holding management or
disposal of any property other than
securities; or

to enter into or offer to enter into an
agreement the purpose or pretended purpose
of which is to secure a profit to any of the
parties by reference to fluctuations in the
value of any property other than securities—

Any person guilty of conspiracy to commit any
offence against the last preceding subsection shall
be punishable as if he had committed such an
offence.

In this section unless inconsistent with the context
or subject-matter—
corporation means any body corporate whether
incorporated in Victoria or elsewhere;
debentures means any debentures debenture stock
or bonds of a corporation, whether
constituting a charge on the assets of the
corporation or not;
securities means—
and includes rights or interests (whether
described as units or otherwise) which may
be acquired under any trust scheme under
which all property for the time being subject
to any trust created in pursuance of the
scheme consists of such securities as are
mentioned in paragraph (a)(b) or (c) of this
interpretation;
shares means shares in the share capital of a
corporation or stock of a corporation.

history.raw: S. 191(3) def. of securities amended by No. 25/2023 s. 7(Sch. 1 item 6.1).

nodes.text:
shares or debentures or rights or
interests (whether described as units or
otherwise) in any shares or debentures;
or

securities of the Government of any
part of His Majesty's dominions or the
Government of any foreign state; or

rights (whether actual or contingent) in
respect of money lent to or deposited
with any corporation—

history.raw: Pt 1 Div. 2AA (Heading and ss 192A–192E) inserted by No. 22/2009 s. 3.

nodes.heading: Definitions
nodes.text: In this Division—

nodes.heading: identification documentation
nodes.text:
means a document
or other thing that—

contains or incorporates identification
information; and

is capable of being used by a person for
the purpose of pretending to be, or
passing themself off as, another person
(whether living or dead, or real or
fictitious);

nodes.heading: identification information
nodes.text:
means information
relating to a person (whether living or dead,
or real or fictitious) that is capable of being
used (whether alone or in conjunction with
other information) to identify, or purportedly
identify, the person, being information such
as—

a name, address, date of birth or place
of birth;

information as to the person's marital
status;

information that identifies another
person as a relative of the person;

a driver licence or driver licence
number;
a passport or passport number;
biometric data;
a voice print;

a credit or debit card, its number or data
stored or encrypted on it;

a financial account number, user name
or password;
a digital signature;

an Australian Business Number within
the meaning of the A New Tax System
(Australian Business Number) Act
1999 of the Commonwealth.

nodes.heading: Making, using or supplying identification information

nodes.text:
A person, who makes, uses or supplies
identification information (that is not
identification information that relates to that
person), and—
is guilty of an offence and liable to level 6
imprisonment (5 years maximum).

who is aware that, or aware that there is a
substantial risk that, the information is
identification information; and

who intends to use or supply the information
to commit an indictable offence, or to
facilitate the commission of an indictable
offence—
See section 426 for an alternative verdict for this offence.

A person may be found guilty of an offence
against this section even if the commission of the
indictable offence is impossible.

It is not a defence to a charge for an offence
against this section that the person to whom the
identification information relates consented to the
making, use or supply of the identification
information.

A person, who possesses identification
information (that is not identification information
that relates to the person), and—
is guilty of an offence and liable to imprisonment
for a term not exceeding 3 years.

who is aware that, or aware that there is a
substantial risk that, the information is
identification information; and

who intends to use the information to
commit an indictable offence, or to facilitate
the commission of an indictable offence—

A person may be found guilty of an offence
against this section even if the commission of the
indictable offence is impossible.

It is not a defence to a charge for an offence
against this section that the person to whom the
identification information relates consented to the
possession of the identification information.

nodes.heading: Possession of equipment used to make etc. identification documentation

nodes.text:
A person, who possesses equipment that is
capable of being used to make, use, supply or
retain identification documentation, and—
is guilty of an offence and liable to imprisonment
for a term not exceeding 3 years.

who intends to use, or who intends that
another person will use, the equipment to
make, use, supply or retain identification
documentation; and

who intends to use any such identification
documentation to commit an indictable
offence or to facilitate the commission of an
indictable offence—

A person may be found guilty of an offence
against this section even if the commission of the
indictable offence is impossible.

nodes.heading: Not an offence to attempt to commit an identity crime offence
nodes.text:
It is not an offence to attempt to commit an
offence against section 192B, 192C or 192D.

history.raw: Pt 1 Div. 2A (Heading and ss 193–195A) inserted by No. 104/2003 s. 3.
New s. 193 inserted by No. 104/2003 s. 3.

nodes.text: In this Division—

nodes.heading: deal with
nodes.text:
includes receive, possess, conceal or
dispose of;

nodes.heading: instrument of crime
nodes.text:
means property that is used
in the commission of, or used to facilitate the
commission of—

an offence referred to in Schedule 1 to
the Confiscation Act 1997; or

an offence against a law of the
Commonwealth that may be dealt with
as an indictable offence (even if it may,
in some circumstances, be dealt with as
a summary offence); or

an offence against a law of another
State, a Territory or a country outside
Australia that would have constituted
an offence referred to in paragraph (a)
if it had been committed in Victoria;

nodes.heading: proceeds of crime
nodes.text:
means property that is derived
or realised, directly or indirectly, by any
person from the commission of—

an offence referred to in Schedule 1 to
the Confiscation Act 1997; or

an offence against a law of the
Commonwealth that may be dealt with
as an indictable offence (even if it may,
in some circumstances, be dealt with as
a summary offence); or

an offence against a law of another
State, a Territory or a country outside
Australia that would have constituted
an offence referred to in paragraph (a)
if it had been committed in Victoria;

nodes.heading: property
nodes.text:
includes money and all other property
real or personal including things in action
and other intangible property.
For the purposes of the definitions of instrument

nodes.heading: of crime
nodes.text:
and proceeds of crime, it is necessary to
prove facts that constitute one or more offences
referred to in paragraph (a), (b) or (c) of those
definitions but the particulars of an offence need
not be proven.

history.raw: New s. 194 inserted by No. 104/2003 s. 3.

nodes.text:
A person must not deal with proceeds of crime—
Penalty: Level 3 imprisonment (20 years
maximum).
knowing that it is proceeds of crime; and

intending to conceal that it is proceeds of
crime.

A person must not deal with proceeds of crime
knowing that it is proceeds of crime.
Penalty: Level 4 imprisonment (15 years
maximum).

A person must not deal with proceeds of crime
being reckless as to whether or not it is proceeds
of crime.
Penalty: Level 5 imprisonment (10 years
maximum).

A person must not deal with proceeds of crime
being negligent as to whether or not it is proceeds
of crime.
Penalty: Level 6 imprisonment (5 years
maximum).

It is a defence to a prosecution for an offence
under this section if the accused satisfies the court
that the accused dealt with the property in order to
assist the enforcement of a law of the
Commonwealth, a State or a Territory.

nodes.heading: Dealing with property suspected of being proceeds of crime
nodes.text:
A person who deals with property if there are
reasonable grounds to suspect that the property is
proceeds of crime is guilty of a summary offence
and liable to level 7 imprisonment (2 years
maximum).

history.raw: New s. 195 inserted by No. 104/2003 s. 3.

nodes.heading: Dealing with property which subsequently becomes an instrument of crime

nodes.text:
A person is guilty of an offence and liable to
level 4 imprisonment (15 years maximum) if—

the person deals with property intending that
the property will become an instrument of
crime; and

the property subsequently becomes an
instrument of crime.

A person is guilty of an offence and liable to
level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum) if—

the person deals with property being reckless
as to whether or not the property will
become an instrument of crime; and

the property subsequently becomes an
instrument of crime.

A person is guilty of an offence and liable to
level 6 imprisonment (5 years maximum) if—

the person deals with property being
negligent as to whether or not the property
will become an instrument of crime; and

the property subsequently becomes an
instrument of crime.

A prosecution for an offence under this section
must not be commenced without the consent of
the Director of Public Prosecutions.

It is a defence to a prosecution for an offence
under this section if the accused satisfies the court
that the accused dealt with the property in order to
assist the enforcement of a law of the
Commonwealth, a State or a Territory.

history.raw: Pt 1 Div. 2B (Heading and ss 195B– 195F) inserted by No. 20/2013 s. 3.

nodes.text: In this Division—

nodes.heading: bet
nodes.text: includes—
place, accept or withdraw a bet; and

cause a bet to be placed, accepted or
withdrawn;

nodes.heading: causing a financial disadvantage

nodes.text:
causing a financial disadvantage to
another person; and

inducing a third person to do something
that results in another person suffering
a financial disadvantage—

nodes.heading: conduct
nodes.text: means an act or omission to do an act;

nodes.heading: conduct that corrupts or would corrupt a betting outcome of an event or an event contingency
nodes.text: means conduct that—

path.definition: conduct that corrupts or would corrupt a betting outcome of an event or an event contingency

nodes.text:
affects or, if engaged in, would or
would be likely to affect the outcome of
any type of betting on the event or
event contingency; and

path.definition: conduct that corrupts or would corrupt a betting outcome of an event or an event contingency

nodes.text:
is contrary to the standards of integrity
that a reasonable person would expect
of persons in a position to affect the
outcome of any type of betting on the
event or event contingency;

path.definition: conduct that corrupts or would corrupt a betting outcome of an event or an event contingency

nodes.heading: encourage
nodes.text:
includes incite, induce, persuade, urge,
threaten or pressure;

nodes.heading: engage in conduct
nodes.text: means—
do an act; or
omit to do an act;

nodes.heading: event
nodes.text:
means an event (whether it takes place in
Victoria or elsewhere) on which it is lawful
to bet under a law of Victoria, another State,
a Territory or the Commonwealth;

nodes.heading: event contingency
nodes.text:
means a contingency
connected to an event, being a contingency
on which it is lawful to bet under a law of
Victoria, another State, a Territory or the
Commonwealth;

nodes.heading: obtaining a financial advantage
nodes.text:
includes—
whether the financial advantage is permanent
or temporary.

obtaining a financial advantage for
oneself or another person; and

inducing a third person to do something
that results in obtaining a financial
advantage for oneself or for another
person; and

retaining a financial advantage that one
has—

In a proceeding for an offence against this
Division, an accused will be taken to have
intended to obtain a financial advantage, or cause
a financial disadvantage, if, and only if, it is
proved that the accused—

intended to obtain a financial advantage, or
to cause a financial disadvantage, in
connection with betting on an event or event
contingency; or

was aware that another person intended to
obtain a financial advantage, or to cause a
financial disadvantage, in connection with
betting on an event or event contingency as a
result of the conduct that is the subject of the
charge.

In a proceeding for an offence against this
Division, it is not necessary to prove that a
financial advantage was actually obtained or a
financial disadvantage was actually caused.

nodes.heading: Engaging in conduct that corrupts or would corrupt a betting outcome of event or event contingency
nodes.text:
A person must not engage in conduct that corrupts
or would corrupt a betting outcome of an event or
event contingency—
Penalty: level 5 imprisonment (10 years
maximum).

knowing that, or being reckless as to
whether, the conduct corrupts or would
corrupt a betting outcome of the event or the
event contingency; and

intending to obtain a financial advantage, or
to cause a financial disadvantage, in
connection with any betting on the event or
the event contingency.

nodes.heading: Facilitating conduct that corrupts or would corrupt a betting outcome of event or event contingency

nodes.text:
A person must not offer to engage in, or
encourage another person to engage in, conduct
that corrupts or would corrupt a betting outcome
of an event or event contingency—
Penalty: level 5 imprisonment (10 years
maximum).

knowing that, or being reckless as to
whether, the conduct corrupts or would
corrupt a betting outcome of the event or
event contingency; and

intending to obtain a financial advantage, or
to cause a financial disadvantage, in
connection with any betting on the event or
the event contingency.

A person must not enter into an agreement or
arrangement in respect of conduct that corrupts or
would corrupt a betting outcome of an event or
event contingency—
Penalty: level 5 imprisonment (10 years
maximum).

knowing that, or being reckless as to
whether, the conduct the subject of the
agreement or arrangement corrupts or would
corrupt a betting outcome of the event or
event contingency; and

intending to obtain a financial advantage, or
to cause a financial disadvantage, in
connection with any betting on the event or
the event contingency.

A person must not encourage another person to
conceal from a relevant authority conduct, or an
agreement or arrangement in respect of conduct,
that corrupts or would corrupt a betting outcome
of an event or event contingency—
Penalty: level 5 imprisonment (10 years
maximum).

knowing that, or being reckless as to
whether, the conduct corrupts or would
corrupt a betting outcome of the event or
event contingency; and

history.raw: S. 195E(2)(a) substituted by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.8).

nodes.text:
intending to obtain a financial advantage, or
cause a financial disadvantage, in connection
with any betting on the event or event
contingency.
In this section relevant authority means—
a police officer; or

a body that has the official function of
controlling, regulating or supervising an
event or betting on an event; or

any other authority of a kind prescribed by
regulation.

nodes.heading: Use of corrupt conduct information for betting purposes

nodes.text:
A person who—
must not, if the information is relevant to the
bet—
Penalty: level 5 imprisonment (10 years
maximum).

possesses information in connection with an
event or event contingency about conduct
that corrupts or would corrupt a betting
outcome of the event or event contingency;
and

knows that, or is reckless as to whether, the
information is about conduct that corrupts or
would corrupt a betting outcome of the event
or event contingency—
bet on the event or event contingency; or

encourage another person to bet on the event
or event contingency in a particular way; or

communicate the information, or cause the
information to be communicated, to another
person who the first person knows or ought
reasonably to know would, or would be
likely to, bet on the event or event
contingency.

In a proceeding for an offence against
subsection (1)(d) or (e), it is not necessary to
prove that the other person actually bet on the
event or event contingency concerned.

nodes.heading: Offences against public order and grossly offensive public conduct

history.raw: Pt 1 Div. 2C (Heading) amended by No. 35/2022 s. 3.
Pt 1 Div. 2C (Heading and ss 195G–195I) inserted by No. 32/2017 s. 8.

nodes.heading: Abolition of certain common law offences against public order
nodes.text:
The offences at common law of affray, rout and
riot are abolished.

A person who uses or threatens unlawful violence
and whose conduct would cause a person of
reasonable firmness present at the scene to be
terrified commits an offence and is liable to—
Engaging in unlawful fighting with another person.
level 6 imprisonment (5 years maximum); or

imprisonment for 7 years if, at the time
of committing the offence, the person is
wearing a face covering used primarily—
to conceal the person's identity; or

to protect the person from the effects
of a crowd-controlling substance.
Example of unlawful violence
A person is guilty of an offence under subsection

only if the person intends to use or threaten
violence or is reckless as to whether the person's
conduct involves the use of violence or threatens
violence.

For the purposes of subsection (1), a threat
of unlawful violence must involve more than
words alone.

An offence under subsection (1) may be
committed—
in private as well as public places; and

whether or not a person of reasonable
firmness is present at the scene.

For the purpose of subsection (1), if 2 or more
persons use or threaten unlawful violence—

it is the conduct of them taken together that
must be considered; and

it is immaterial whether or not those
persons use or threaten unlawful violence
simultaneously.

Violent disorder occurs where 6 or more persons
(the participants) who are present together use or
threaten unlawful violence with a common goal or
intention and the conduct of them, taken together,
causes injury to another person or causes damage
to property.
For the purposes of subsection (1)—

violent disorder may occur in private
as well as public places; and

it is immaterial whether or not the
participants use or threaten unlawful
violence simultaneously; and

the common goal or intention may
be inferred from the conduct of the
participants.

A participant in violent disorder commits
an offence and is liable to—

level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum);
or

level 4 imprisonment (15 years maximum) if,
at the time of committing the offence, the
participant is wearing a face covering used
primarily—
to conceal the participant's identity; or

to protect the participant from
the effects of a crowd-controlling
substance.
A person is guilty of an offence under subsection

only if the person intends to use or threaten
violence or is reckless as to whether the person's
conduct involves the use of violence or threatens
violence.

Subsection (4) does not affect the determination
for the purposes of subsection (1) of the number
of persons who are engaging in the conduct
referred to in subsection (1).

nodes.heading: Abolition of common law offence of outraging public decency
nodes.text:
The offence at common law of outraging public
decency is abolished.
A person (the offender) commits an offence if—

the offender engages in conduct that grossly
offends community standards of acceptable
conduct; and
that conduct—
is engaged in at a public place; or

is seen or heard by a person in a public
place; and

the offender knows that, or is reckless as to
whether—

the place at which the conduct is
engaged in is a public place; or

the conduct is likely to be seen or heard
by a person in a public place; and

the offender knows, or a reasonable person
would know, that the conduct would likely
grossly offend community standards of
acceptable conduct.

A person who commits an offence against
subsection (1) is liable to level 6 imprisonment
(5 years maximum).

A reference in subsection (1) to conduct being
seen or heard does not include seeing or hearing it
by using electronic communication.

A person's conduct does not grossly offend
community standards of acceptable conduct just
because—

the person uses language that is profane,
indecent or obscene; or
the person is intoxicated.

It is a defence to a charge for an offence against
subsection (1) if the accused engaged in the
conduct reasonably and in good faith—

in the performance, exhibition or distribution
of an artistic work; or

in the course of any statement or publication
made, or discussion or debate held, or any
other conduct engaged in, for—

a genuine political, academic,
educational, artistic, religious, cultural
or scientific purpose; or

a purpose that is in the public interest;
or

in making or publishing a fair and accurate
report of any event or matter of public
interest.

In this section—
public place means—

a public place within the meaning of
section 3 of the Summary Offences
Act 1966; or

a non-Government school within the
meaning of section 1.1.3(1) of the
Education and Training Reform
Act 2006; or

a post-secondary education institution
within the meaning of section 1.1.3(1)
of the Education and Training
Reform Act 2006.

nodes.heading: Consent of Director of Public Prosecutions required
nodes.text:
A prosecution for an offence against section
195K(1) must not be commenced without the
consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

history.raw: Pt 1 Div. 2D (Heading and ss 195M– 195R) inserted by No. 11/2025 s. 4.

nodes.heading: Definitions
nodes.text: In this Division—

nodes.heading: disability
nodes.text:
has the same meaning as in section 4(1)
of the Equal Opportunity Act 2010;

nodes.heading: gender identity
protected attribute
nodes.text:
means any of the following
attributes—
disability;
gender identity;
race;
religious belief or activity;
sex;
sex characteristics;
sexual orientation;

personal association (whether as a
relative or otherwise) with a person
who is identified by reference to any of
the above attributes;

nodes.heading: race
nodes.text:
has the same meaning as in section 4(1) of
the Equal Opportunity Act 2010;

nodes.heading: religious belief or activity
sex characteristics
sexual orientation
nodes.text:
has the same meaning as in
section 4(1) of the Equal Opportunity
Act 2010.

nodes.heading: Incitement on ground of protected attribute

nodes.text: A person commits an offence if—

the person engages in conduct that is likely
to incite hatred against, serious contempt for,
revulsion towards or severe ridicule of,
another person or a group of persons; and

the person engages in the conduct on the
ground of a protected attribute of the other
person or the group; and
the person either—

intends that conduct to incite hatred
against, serious contempt for, revulsion
towards or severe ridicule of, the other
person or the group; or

believes that conduct will probably
incite hatred against, serious contempt
for, revulsion towards or severe ridicule
of, the other person or the group.

A person who commits an offence against
subsection (1) is liable to 3 years imprisonment.

For the purposes of subsection (1), the conduct
may be constituted by a single occasion or by a
number of occasions over a period of time.

If conduct engaged in from outside Victoria is
alleged to constitute an offence against subsection

, every person against whom the offence is
alleged to have been committed must have been in
Victoria when at least some of the conduct was
engaged in for the conduct to constitute that
offence.

Conduct that—
does not constitute an offence against subsection
is engaged in from outside Victoria; and

is against a group of persons that is defined
solely by the possession of a protected
attribute—

If a person in another State engages in conduct that is
against all people of a certain race, whether or not those
people are within Victoria, that conduct does not constitute
an offence against subsection (1).

If any of the conduct alleged to constitute an
offence against subsection (1) is engaged in from
within Victoria, it does not matter whether a
person against whom the offence is alleged to
have been committed was outside Victoria at that
time.

nodes.heading: Threaten physical harm or property damage on ground of protected attribute

nodes.text: A person commits an offence if—
the person threatens—

physical harm towards another person
or a group of persons; or

to damage property of, or otherwise
related to, another person or a group of
persons; and

the person threatens the physical harm or the
property damage on the ground of a
protected attribute of the other person or the
group; and
the person either—

intends that the other person or a person
of the group will believe the threat will
be carried out; or

believes that the other person or a
person of the group will probably
believe the threat will be carried out.

A person who commits an offence against
subsection (1) is liable to level 6 imprisonment
(5 years maximum).

If a threat made from outside Victoria is alleged to
constitute an offence against subsection (1), the
following persons or property must have been in
Victoria when the threat was made for the threat
to constitute that offence—

in the case of a threat to physically harm a
person or a group of persons, that person or
group; or

in the case of a threat to damage property,
that property.

If a threat that is alleged to constitute an offence
against subsection (1) is made from within
Victoria, it does not matter whether the following
persons or property were outside Victoria at that
time—

in the case of a threat to physically harm a
person, that person; or

in the case of a threat to physically harm a
group of persons, any of those persons; or

in the case of a threat to damage property,
that property.

nodes.heading: Irrelevant whether incorrect about protected attribute
nodes.text:
In determining whether a person has committed an
offence against section 195N(1) or 195O(1), it is
irrelevant that the person was incorrect about—

a protected attribute of the other person or
group of persons; or

whether the other person or group of persons
had a particular protected attribute.

nodes.heading: Prosecution of offences
nodes.text:
A prosecution for an offence against
section 195N(1) or 195O(1)—

history.raw: S. 195Q inserted by No. 11/2025 s. 4, substituted by No. 8/2026 s. 3.

nodes.text:
may only be commenced by the Director of
Public Prosecutions or a police officer; and

if the prosecution is of a person under the
age of 18 years, may only be commenced by
a police officer with the consent of the
Director of Public Prosecutions.

nodes.heading: Criminal liability of officers of bodies corporate— accessorial liability

nodes.text:
If a body corporate commits an offence against a
provision specified in subsection (2), an officer of
the body corporate also commits an offence
against the provision if the officer—

authorised or permitted the commission of
the offence by the body corporate; or

was knowingly concerned in any way
(whether by act or omission) in the
commission of the offence by the body
corporate.

For the purposes of subsection (1), the following
provisions are specified—
section 195N(1);
section 195O(1).

Without limiting any other defence available to
the officer, an officer of a body corporate may
rely on a defence that would be available to the
body corporate if it were charged with the offence
with which the officer is charged and, in doing so,
the officer bears the same burden of proof that the
body corporate would bear.

An officer of a body corporate may commit an
offence against a provision specified in subsection

whether or not the body corporate has been
prosecuted for, or found guilty of, an offence
against that provision.

In this section—
body corporate has the same meaning as
corporation has in section 57A of the
Corporations Act;
officer, in relation to a body corporate, means—

a person who is an officer (as defined
by section 9 of the Corporations Act) of
the body corporate; or

a person (other than a person referred to
in paragraph (a)), by whatever name
called, who is concerned in, or takes
part in, the management of the body
corporate.

This section does not affect the operation of
Subdivision (1) of Division 1 of Part II of this Act.

history.raw: Pt 1 Div. 2E (Heading and ss 195S– 195W) inserted by No. 29/2025 s. 3.

nodes.text: For the purposes of this Division—

nodes.heading: material
nodes.text: means—

any electronic material, including data
from which text, images or sound may
be generated; or
any other thing of any kind;
See also subsection (2).

nodes.heading: publish
nodes.text: has the meaning given by section 195T;

nodes.heading: relevant offence
nodes.text:
has the meaning given by
section 195U.

For the purposes of this Division, an image may
be still, moving, recorded or unrecorded.

For the purposes of this Division, to publish
material means to make the material available to
the public or a section of the public—
by electronic communication; or

by sending, supplying, exhibiting,
transmitting or communicating the material
by any other means.

A person does not publish material by making the
material available to only one other person.

For the purposes of this Division, a relevant
offence is—

an offence against any of the following
sections—

section 74 (theft), if the property stolen
is a motor vehicle;
section 75 (robbery);
section 75A (armed robbery);
section 76 (burglary);
section 77 (aggravated burglary);
section 77A (home invasion);

section 77B (aggravated home
invasion);
section 79 (carjacking);
section 79A (aggravated carjacking);
section 195H (affray);
section 195I (violent disorder); or

an offence against section 321G (incitement)
or 321M (attempt) in relation to an offence
referred to in paragraph (a).
However, an offence referred to in subsection

(a) or (b) is not a relevant offence if it is
committed before the commencement of
section 195V.

For the purposes of subsection (2), if an offence is
committed—
the offence is committed before that
commencement.

at an unidentified time between 2 dates, one
before and one on or after the
commencement of section 195V; or

throughout a period during which
section 195V commences—

nodes.heading: Publishing material about the commission of a relevant offence

nodes.text:
A person must not—
Penalty: Level 7 imprisonment (2 years
maximum).

publish or cause to be published material that
depicts, describes or otherwise indicates the
commission of a relevant offence by the
person; and

undertake or cause that publication with the
intention of attracting attention to the
commission of that offence.

An offence against subsection (1) is a summary
offence.

Without limiting subsection (1)(a), material that
depicts, describes or otherwise indicates the
commission of a relevant offence includes
material that depicts or describes—

anything done in the course of committing
the relevant offence; or

property obtained from committing the
relevant offence; or

damage or harm caused by committing the
relevant offence.

A person is not liable for an offence against
subsection (1) unless the person is found guilty of
the relevant offence referred to in subsection

(a), whether in the same proceeding or in an
earlier proceeding.

Nothing in subsection (4) requires that a person
must have been found guilty of a relevant offence
before they may be charged with an offence
against subsection (1) in respect of that relevant
offence.

nodes.heading: Issue of search warrant by magistrate in respect of performance crime offence

nodes.text:
Section 465 applies to and in respect of an offence
against section 195V(1) as if it were an indictable
offence.

The other provisions of Subdivision (31) of
Division 1 of Part III apply in relation to a warrant
issued under section 465, as applied by subsection

, in the same way that those provisions apply
in relation to any other warrant issued under
section 465.

nodes.heading: Use of knives in the commission of certain indictable offences

history.raw: Pt 1 Div. 2F (Heading and s. 195X) inserted by No. 54/2025 s. 9.

nodes.heading: Use of knives in the commission of certain indictable offences

nodes.text:
A person must not use a knife in committing a
relevant offence.
Penalty: 3 years imprisonment.

Each of the following is a relevant offence for the
purposes of this section—

an offence against section 16 (causing
serious injury intentionally);

an offence against section 17 (causing
serious injury recklessly);

an offence against section 18 (causing injury
intentionally or recklessly);

an offence against section 31(1) constituted
by the conduct described in paragraph (a) of
that provision (assaulting, or threatening to
assault, with intent to commit an indictable
offence);
an offence against section 195H (affray);

an offence against section 195I (violent
disorder).

A person is not liable for an offence against
subsection (1) unless the person is found guilty of
the relevant offence referred to in that subsection.

Nothing in subsection (3) requires that a person
must have been found guilty of a relevant offence
before they may be charged with an offence
against subsection (1) in respect of that relevant
offence.

nodes.text: In this subdivision—

nodes.heading: property
nodes.text:
means property of a tangible nature,
whether real or personal, including money
and including wild creatures which have
been tamed or are ordinarily kept in captivity
and any other wild creatures or their
carcasses if, but only if, they have been
reduced into possession which has not been
lost or abandoned or are in the course of
being reduced into possession.

For the purposes of this subdivision property shall
be treated as belonging to any person—
having the custody or control of it;

having in it any proprietary right or interest
(not being an equitable interest arising only
from an agreement to transfer or grant an
interest); or
having a charge on it.

For the purposes of this subdivision property
which is subject to a trust shall be treated as
belonging to the trustee or trustees and the person
or persons who have a right to enforce the trust.

For the purposes of this subdivision property of a
corporation sole shall be treated as belonging to
the corporation notwithstanding a vacancy in the
corporation.

history.raw: S. 197 repealed by No. 9228 s. 2(1)(c), new s. 197 inserted by No. 9228 s. 2(1)(d).

nodes.text:
A person who intentionally and without lawful
excuse destroys or damages any property
belonging to another or to himself and another
shall be guilty of an indictable offence and liable
to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).

A person who intentionally and without lawful
excuse destroys or damages any property,
intending by the destruction or damage to
endanger the life of another, shall be guilty of an
indictable offence and liable to level 4
imprisonment (15 years maximum).

A person who dishonestly, with a view to gain for
himself or another, destroys or damages any
property shall be guilty of an indictable offence
and liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years
maximum).

For the purposes of subsections (1) and (2) a
person who destroys or damages property shall be
taken as doing so intentionally if, but only if—

his purpose or one of his purposes is to
destroy or damage property; or

he knows or believes that his conduct is
more likely than not to result in destruction
of or damage to property.

For the purposes of subsection (2), a person who
destroys or damages property shall be treated as
intending thereby to endanger the life of another
if, but only if—

his purpose or one of his purposes is to
endanger the life of another by the
destruction or damage; or

he knows or believes that the life of another
is more likely than not to be endangered by
the destruction or damage.

An offence against this section committed by
destroying or damaging property by fire shall be
charged as arson.

A person guilty of arson is liable to level 4
imprisonment (15 years maximum) despite
anything to the contrary in this section.

history.raw: S. 197(7) inserted by No. 95/1994 s. 4, amended by No. 48/1997 s. 60(1)(Sch. 1 item 70(b)).

nodes.heading: Arson causing death
nodes.text:
A person who commits arson as defined in
section 197 and thereby causes the death of
another person is guilty of an indictable offence.
Penalty: Level 2 imprisonment (25 years
maximum).

history.raw: Note to s. 197A inserted by No. 65/2016 s. 20(19).

nodes.text:
An offence against this section is a category 2 offence under the
Sentencing Act 1991. See subsection (2H) of section 5 of that Act
for the requirement to impose a custodial order for this offence
unless the circumstances set out in paragraphs (a) to (e) of that
subsection exist.

nodes.heading: Threats to destroy or damage property
nodes.text:
A person who without lawful excuse makes to
another a threat—
shall, if he made the threat with the purpose of
causing the other to fear that it would be carried
out, be guilty of an indictable offence and liable to
level 6 imprisonment (5 years maximum).

nodes.text:
to destroy or damage any property belonging
to that other or a third person or to himself
and that other or a third person; or

to destroy or damage his own property in a
way which he knows or believes is more
likely than not to endanger the life of that
other or a third person—

nodes.heading: Possessing anything with intent to destroy or damage property
nodes.text:
A person who has anything in his custody or
under his control—
shall be guilty of an indictable offence and liable
to level 6 imprisonment (5 years maximum).

history.raw: S. 201 repealed by No. 9228 s. 2(1)(c), new s. 201 inserted by No. 9228 s. 2(1)(d).

nodes.text:
This section applies to any offence under
section 197(1), 198(a) or 199(a)(i).

A person charged with an offence to which this
section applies shall, whether or not he would be
treated for the purposes of this subdivision as
having a lawful excuse apart from this subsection,
be treated for those purposes as having a lawful
excuse—

if at the time of the conduct alleged to
constitute the offence he believed—

that the property in question belonged
solely to himself;

that he held a right or interest in the
property in question which authorized
him to engage in the conduct; or

that the person or persons whom he
believed to be entitled to consent to the
destruction or damage in question had
so consented or would have so
consented if he or they had known the
circumstances of the destruction or
damage; or

if he engaged in the conduct alleged to
constitute the offence in order to protect
property belonging to himself or another or a
right or interest in property which was or
which he believed to be vested in himself or
another, and at the time of such conduct he
believed—

that the property, right or interest which
he sought to protect was in immediate
need of protection; and

that the means of protection adopted or
proposed to be adopted were or would
be reasonable having regard to all the
circumstances.

For the purposes of this section it is immaterial
whether a belief is justified or not if it is honestly
held.

For the purposes of subsection (2) a right or
interest in property includes any right or privilege
in or over land, whether created by grant, licence
or otherwise.

This section shall not be construed as taking away
or otherwise affecting any other defence
recognized by law as a defence to criminal
charges.

nodes.heading: Intentionally or recklessly causing a bushfire

nodes.text:
A person who—
is guilty of an offence and liable to level 4
imprisonment (15 years maximum).
intentionally or recklessly causes a fire; and

is reckless as to the spread of the fire to
vegetation on property belonging to
another—

For the purposes of subsection (1)(b),
circumstances in which a person is not to be taken
to be reckless as to the spread of a fire include the
following—

the person caused the fire in the course of
carrying out a fire prevention, fire
suppression or other land management
activity; and
at the time the activity was carried out—

there was in force a provision made by
or under an Act or by a Code of
Practice approved under an Act, that
regulated or otherwise applied to the
carrying out of the activity and the
person in carrying out that activity
acted in accordance with the provision;
and

the person believed that his or her
conduct in carrying out the activity was
justified having regard to all of the
circumstances.

For the purposes of subsection (2)(b)(ii) it is
sufficient that a person honestly believed that the
conduct was justified.
In this section—
a reference to causing a fire includes—
lighting a fire;
maintaining a fire;

failing to contain a fire, except where
the fire was lit by another person or the
fire is beyond the control of the person
who lit the fire;

spread of the fire means spread of the fire
beyond the capacity of the person who
caused the fire to extinguish it.

nodes.heading: Jurisdiction of magistrates' courts
nodes.text:
No rule of law ousting the jurisdiction of the
Magistrates' Court to try offences where a dispute
of title to property is involved shall preclude the
Magistrates' Court from trying offences mentioned
in this subdivision or from trying any other
offences of destroying or damaging property.

nodes.heading: Injuries to buildings &c. by rioters and forcible entries and detainers

history.raw: Pt 1 Div. 3 Subdiv. (2) (Heading and ss 204, 205) repealed by No. 9228 s. 2(1)(c).
New Pt 1 Div. 3 Subdiv. (2) (Heading) inserted by No. 9228 s. 2(1)(e).

nodes.text:
Whosoever is one of any persons riotously and
tumultuously assembled together to the
disturbance of the public peace who unlawfully
and with force demolish or pull down or destroy
or begin to demolish pull down or destroy any
church chapel meeting-house or other place of
divine worship, or any house stable coach-house
outhouse warehouse office shop mill malthouse
hop-oast barn granary shed hovel or fold, or any
building or erection used in farming land or in
carrying on any trade or manufacture or any
branch thereof, or any building other than such as
are in this section before mentioned belonging to
the King or the Government of Victoria or to any
municipal council or belonging to any university,
or devoted or dedicated to public use or ornament,
or erected or maintained by public subscription or
contribution, or any machinery (whether fixed or
movable) prepared for or employed in any
manufacture or any steam-engine or other engine
for sinking working ventilating or draining any
mine, or any staith building or erection used in
conducting the business of any mine or any bridge
waggon-way tramway trunk or shoot for
conveying minerals from any mine, shall be guilty
of an indictable offence, and shall be liable to
level 4 imprisonment (15 years maximum).

Whosoever is one of any persons riotously and
tumultuously assembled together to the
disturbance of the public peace who unlawfully
and with force injure or damage any such place
building or erection or thing as is in the last
subsection mentioned, shall be guilty of an
indictable offence, and shall be liable to level 6
imprisonment (5 years maximum).

No person being in actual possession of land for a
period of less than three years by himself or his
predecessors shall without colour of right hold
possession of it in a manner likely to cause a
breach of the peace or a reasonable apprehension
of a breach of the peace against a person entitled
by law to the possession of the land and able and
willing to afford reasonable information as to his
being so entitled.

Every person who is guilty of a contravention of
this section shall be guilty of a summary offence
and liable to level 8 imprisonment (1 year
maximum) or a level 10 fine or both.

nodes.heading: Interference with mines, sea banks &c., railways and navigation aids

history.raw: Pt 1 Div. 3 Subdiv. (3) (Heading) repealed by No. 9228 s. 2(1)(c).
New Pt 1 Div. 3 Subdiv. (3) (Heading) inserted by No. 9228 s. 2(1)(f).

nodes.heading: Conveying water into a mine
nodes.text:
Whosoever unlawfully and maliciously causes any
water to be conveyed or run into any mine or into
any subterraneous passage communicating
therewith with intent thereby to destroy or damage
such mine or to hinder or delay the working
thereof, or with the like intent unlawfully and
maliciously pulls down fills up or obstructs or
damages with intent to destroy obstruct or render
useless any airway waterway drain pit level shaft
or drive of or belonging to any mine, shall be
guilty of an indictable offence, and shall be liable
to level 6 imprisonment (5 years maximum).
This provision shall not extend to any damage
committed underground by any owner of any
adjoining mine in working the same or by any
person duly employed in such working.

nodes.heading: Removing etc. piles of sea banks
nodes.text:
Whosoever unlawfully and maliciously cuts off
draws up or removes any piles chalk or other
materials fixed in the ground and used for
securing any sea bank or sea wall or the bank dam
or wall of any river canal drain aqueduct marsh
reservoir pool port harbor dock quay wharf jetty
or lock, or unlawfully and maliciously opens or
draws up any floodgate or sluice or does any other
injury or mischief to any navigable river or canal
with intent to obstruct or prevent the carrying on
completing or maintaining the navigation thereof,
shall be guilty of an indictable offence, and shall
be liable to level 6 imprisonment (5 years
maximum).

nodes.heading: Placing things on railways to obstruct or overturn engine etc.16
nodes.text:
Whosoever unlawfully and maliciously puts
places casts or throws upon or across any railway
any wood stone or other matter or thing, or
unlawfully and maliciously takes up removes or
displaces any rail sleeper or other thing belonging
to any railway, or unlawfully and maliciously
turns moves or diverts any points or other
machinery belonging to any railway, or
unlawfully and maliciously makes or shows hides
or removes any signal or light upon or near to any
railway, or unlawfully and maliciously does or
causes to be done any other matter or thing with
intent in any such case to obstruct upset overthrow
injure or destroy any engine tender carriage or
truck on such railway, shall be guilty of an
indictable offence, and shall be liable to level 5
imprisonment (10 years maximum).

nodes.heading: Obstructing engine, carriage etc. on railway17
nodes.text:
Whosoever by any unlawful act or by any wilful
omission or neglect obstructs or causes to be
obstructed any engine or carriage on any railway,
or aids or assists therein, shall be guilty of a
summary offence, and shall be liable to level 7
imprisonment (2 years maximum).

nodes.heading: Altering signals or exhibiting false ones
nodes.text:
Whosoever unlawfully masks alters or removes
any light or signal or exhibits any false light or
signal with intent to bring any ship vessel or boat
into danger, or unlawfully and maliciously does
anything tending to the immediate loss or
destruction of any ship vessel or boat and for
which no punishment is hereinbefore provided,
shall be guilty of an indictable offence, and shall
be liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years
maximum).

nodes.heading: Removing buoy etc.
nodes.text:
Whosoever unlawfully and maliciously cuts away
casts adrift removes alters defaces sinks or
destroys or in any other manner injures or
conceals, or unlawfully and maliciously does any
act with intent to cut away cast adrift remove alter
deface sink destroy, or in any other manner injure
or conceal, any boat buoy rope perch or mark used
or intended for the guidance of seamen or the
purpose of navigation, shall be guilty of an
indictable offence, and shall be liable to level 6
imprisonment (5 years maximum).

history.raw: Pt 1 Div. 3 Subdivs (4)(5) (Headings and ss 208–210) repealed by No. 9228 s. 2(1)(c).
New Pt 1 Div. 3 Subdiv. (4) (Heading) inserted by No. 9228 s. 2(1)(g).

nodes.heading: Endangering safe operation of an aircraft
nodes.text:
Any person who does any act or thing with intent
to prejudice the safe operation of an aircraft shall
be guilty of an indictable offence and liable to
level 4 imprisonment (15 years maximum).

history.raw: S. 246A inserted by No. 7088 s. 2(d), amended by Nos 9576 s. 11(1), 49/1991 s. 119(1) (Sch. 2 item 49), 48/1997 s. 60(1)(Sch. 1 item 79).

nodes.heading: Setting fire etc. to aircraft
nodes.text:
Any person who unlawfully and maliciously sets
fire to or in any way destroys any aircraft whether
complete or incomplete shall be guilty of an
indictable offence and shall be liable to level 4
imprisonment (15 years maximum).

history.raw: S. 246B inserted by No. 7088 s. 2(d), amended by Nos 9576 s. 11(1), 49/1991 s. 119(1) (Sch. 2 item 53), 48/1997 s. 60(1)(Sch. 1 item 80).

nodes.heading: Endangering safety of aircraft
nodes.text:
Any person who while on board an aircraft does
any act or thing that is likely to endanger the
safety of the aircraft shall be guilty of an
indictable offence and shall be liable to level 5
imprisonment (10 years maximum).

history.raw: S. 246C inserted by No. 7088 s. 2(d), amended by Nos 9576 s. 11(1), 49/1991 s. 119(1) (Sch. 2 item 57), 48/1997 s. 60(1)(Sch. 1 item 81).

nodes.text:
Subject to this section any person who—
shall be guilty of an indictable offence and shall
be liable to level 6 imprisonment (5 years
maximum).

carries or places dangerous goods on board
an aircraft;

delivers dangerous goods to a person for the
purpose of their being placed on board an
aircraft; or

has dangerous goods in his possession on
board an aircraft—
This section does not apply—

to or in relation to any act done with the
consent of the owner or operator of the
aircraft given with a knowledge of the nature
of the goods concerned; or

to or in relation to the carrying or placing of
firearms or ammunition for firearms on
board an aircraft with permission granted
under the Air Navigation Regulations of the
Commonwealth.
In this section dangerous goods means—

firearms, ammunition, weapons and
explosive substances; and

substances or things that, by reason of their
nature or condition, may endanger the safety
of an aircraft or of persons on board an
aircraft.

nodes.heading: Threats to safety of aircraft
nodes.text:
Any person who threatens, states that it is his
intention, or makes a statement from which it
could reasonably be inferred that it is his intention
to destroy damage or endanger the safety of an
aircraft or to kill or injure all or any of the persons
on board an aircraft shall be guilty of an indictable
offence and liable to level 6 imprisonment
(5 years maximum).

history.raw: S. 246E inserted by No. 7088 s. 2(d), amended by Nos 9576 s. 11(1), 49/1991 s. 119(1) (Sch. 2 item 57), 48/1997 s. 60(1)(Sch. 1 item 82).
Pt 1 Div. 3 Subdiv. (5) (Heading) inserted by No. 9228 s. 2(1)(h) (as amended by No. 9427 s. 6(1)).

nodes.heading: False statements
nodes.text:
Any person who makes a statement or conveys
information, being a statement or information that
he knows to be false, to the effect or from which it
could reasonably be inferred that there has been or
is to be a plan, proposal, attempt, conspiracy or
threat to—
shall be guilty of an indictable offence and shall
be liable to level 6 imprisonment (5 years
maximum).

take or exercise control by force or violence
of any building (including any structure in

destroy, damage or endanger the safety

nodes.text: In this Subdivision—

nodes.heading: access
nodes.text:
, in relation to data held in a computer,
means—

the display of the data by the computer
or any other output of the data from the
computer; or

the copying or moving of the data to
any other place in the computer or to a
data storage device; or

in the case of a program, the execution
of the program;

nodes.heading: data
nodes.text: includes—
information in any form; and
any program or part of a program;

nodes.heading: data held in a computer
nodes.text: includes—

data entered or copied into the
computer; and

data held in any removable data storage
device for the time being in the
computer; and

nodes.heading: data storage device
electronic communication
nodes.text:
means a
communication of information in any form
by means of guided or unguided
electromagnetic energy;

nodes.heading: impairment
nodes.text:
, in relation to electronic
communication to or from a computer,
includes—
but does not include a mere interception of
any such communication;

the prevention of any such
communication; and

the impairment of any such
communication on an electronic link or
network used by the computer—

nodes.heading: modification
nodes.text:
, in relation to data held in a
computer, means—
the alteration or removal of the data; or
an addition to the data;

nodes.heading: serious computer offence
nodes.text: means—

an offence against section 247B, 247C
or 247D; or

conduct in another jurisdiction that is
an offence in that jurisdiction and that
would constitute an offence against
section 247B, 247C or 247D if the
conduct occurred in Victoria;

nodes.heading: unauthorised computer function
nodes.text:
means any of
the following—

any unauthorised access to data held in
a computer; or

any unauthorised modification of data
held in a computer; or

any unauthorised impairment of
electronic communication to or from a
computer.

In this Subdivision, a reference to access to data,
modification of data or impairment of electronic
communication is limited to access, modification
or impairment caused (whether directly or
indirectly) by the execution of a function of a
computer.

For the purposes of this Subdivision, access to
data, modification of data or impairment of
electronic communication by a person—

is not unauthorised merely because the
person has an ulterior purpose for that action.

For the purposes of an offence against this
Subdivision, a person causes an unauthorised
computer function if the person's conduct
substantially contributes to the unauthorised
computer function.

nodes.heading: Unauthorised access, modification or impairment with intent to commit serious offence

nodes.text:
A person who causes any unauthorised computer
function—
is guilty of an offence and liable to the same
maximum penalty as applies to the commission of
the serious offence in Victoria.
knowing it is unauthorised; and

with the intention of committing a serious
offence or facilitating the commission of a
serious offence (whether by the person or by
another person)—
In this section serious offence means—

an offence in Victoria punishable on
conviction for a first offence with
imprisonment for a term of 5 years or more;
or

an offence in any other jurisdiction that
would be punishable on conviction for a first
offence with imprisonment for a term of
5 years or more if committed in Victoria.

A person may be found guilty of an offence
against this section—

even if committing the serious offence is
impossible; or

whether the serious offence is to be
committed at the time of the unauthorised
conduct or at a later time.

It is not an offence to attempt to commit an
offence against this section.

nodes.heading: Unauthorised modification of data to cause impairment
nodes.text:
A person who—
is guilty of an offence and liable to level 5
imprisonment (10 years maximum).

causes any unauthorised modification of data
held in a computer; and

knows that the modification is unauthorised;
and

intends by the modification to impair access
to, or to impair the reliability, security or
operation of, any data held in a computer or
is reckless as to any such impairment—

nodes.heading: Unauthorised impairment of electronic communication
nodes.text:
A person who—
is guilty of an offence and liable to level 5
imprisonment (10 years maximum).

causes any unauthorised impairment of
electronic communication to or from a
computer; and

knows that the impairment is unauthorised;
and

intends to impair electronic communication
to or from the computer or is reckless as to
any such impairment—

nodes.heading: Possession of data with intent to commit serious computer offence

nodes.text:
A person who is in possession or control of data—
is guilty of an offence and liable to imprisonment
for a term not exceeding 3 years.

with the intention of committing a serious
computer offence; or

with the intention of facilitating the
commission of a serious computer offence
(whether by the person or by another
person)—

In this section, a reference to a person having
possession or control of data includes a reference
to a person—

having possession of a computer or data
storage device that holds or contains the
data; and

having possession of a document in which
the data is recorded; and

having control of data held in a computer
that is in the possession of another person
(whether the computer is in Victoria or
outside Victoria).

A person may be found guilty of an offence
against this section even if committing the serious
computer offence is impossible.

It is not an offence to attempt to commit an
offence against this section.

nodes.heading: Producing, supplying or obtaining data with intent to commit serious computer offence

nodes.text:
A person who produces, supplies or obtains
data—
is guilty of an offence and liable to imprisonment
for a term not exceeding 3 years.

with the intention of committing a serious
computer offence; or

with the intention of facilitating the
commission of a serious computer offence
(whether by the person or by another
person)—

In this section, a reference to a person producing,
supplying or obtaining data includes a reference to
the person—

producing, supplying or obtaining data held
in a computer or contained in a data storage
device; and

producing, supplying or obtaining a
document in which the data is recorded.

A person may be found guilty of an offence
against this section even if committing the serious
computer offence is impossible.

nodes.heading: Unauthorised access to or modification of restricted data

nodes.text:
A person who—
is guilty of an offence and liable to level 7
imprisonment (2 years maximum).

causes any unauthorised access to or
modification of restricted data held in a
computer; and

knows that the access or modification is
unauthorised; and
intends to cause the access or modification—

An offence against this section is a summary
offence.

In this section restricted data means data held in a
computer to which access is restricted by an
access control system associated with a function
of the computer.

nodes.heading: Unauthorised impairment of data held in computer disk, credit card or other device

nodes.text:
A person who—
is guilty of an offence and liable to level 7
imprisonment (2 years maximum).

causes any unauthorised impairment of the
reliability, security or operation of data held
on a computer disk, credit card or other
device used to store data by electronic
means; and

knows that the impairment is unauthorised;
and
intends to cause the impairment—

An offence against this section is a summary
offence.

For the purposes of this section, impairment of
reliability, security or operation of data is
unauthorised if the person is not entitled to cause
the impairment.

It is immaterial that some or all of the conduct
constituting an offence against this Subdivision
occurred outside Victoria, so long as the computer
or device used to store data by electronic means
affected by the conduct was in Victoria at the time
at which the conduct occurred.

It is immaterial that the computer or device used
to store data by electronic means affected by some
or all of the conduct constituting an offence
against this Subdivision was outside Victoria at
the time the conduct occurred, so long as that
conduct occurred in Victoria.

history.raw: Pt 1 Div. 3 Subdiv. (7) (Heading and ss 247J–247L) inserted by No. 10/2003 s. 6.

nodes.text: In this Subdivision—

nodes.heading: property offence
nodes.text: means—

an offence against Subdivision (1) of
this Division or Division 4; or

conduct in another jurisdiction that is
an offence in that jurisdiction and that
would constitute an offence against
Subdivision (1) of this Division or
Division 4 if the conduct occurred in
Victoria;

nodes.heading: public facility
nodes.text:
means any of the following
(whether publicly or privately owned)—

a government facility, including
premises used by government
employees in connection with official
duties;

a public infrastructure facility,
including a facility providing or
distributing water, sewerage, energy,
fuel, communication or other services
to, or for the benefit of, the public;

a public information system, including
a system used to generate, send,
receive, store or otherwise process
electronic communications;

a public place, including any premises,
land or water open to the public;

nodes.heading: unauthorised computer function
nodes.text:
has the same
meaning as in Subdivision (6).

In this Subdivision damage, in relation to a public
facility, means—

cause damage to the facility or any part of
the facility; or

cause disruption to the use or operation of
the facility.

For the purposes of an offence against this
Subdivision, a person causes any damage or
disruption if the person's conduct substantially
contributes to the damage or disruption.

nodes.heading: Sabotage
nodes.text:
A person who—
is guilty of an offence and liable to level 2
imprisonment (25 years maximum).

damages a public facility by committing a
property offence or by causing an
unauthorised computer function; and
intends to cause—

major disruption to government
functions; or

major disruption to the use of services
by the public; or
major economic loss—

A person who—
is guilty of an offence and liable to level 4
imprisonment (15 years maximum).

makes to another person a threat to damage a
public facility by committing a property
offence or by causing an unauthorised
computer function; and

intends that person to fear that the threat will
be carried out and will cause—

major disruption to government
functions; or

major disruption to the use of services
by the public; or
major economic loss—

In the prosecution of an offence against this
section it is not necessary to prove that the person
threatened actually feared that the threat would be
carried out.
For the purposes of this section—

a threat may be made by any conduct and
may be explicit or implicit, conditional or
unconditional; and

a threat to a person includes a threat to a
group of persons; and

fear that a threat will be carried out includes
apprehension that it will be carried out.

New s. 248 inserted by No. 95/1994 s. 5, amended by Nos 48/1997 s. 60(1)(Sch. 1 item 84), 69/1997 s. 22(6), substituted by No. 65/1998 s. 5.

nodes.text: In this Division—

nodes.heading: contaminate
nodes.text: , in relation to goods, includes—
interfere with the goods; or

making it appear that the goods have
been contaminated or interfered with;

nodes.heading: goods
nodes.text: includes any substance—

whether or not for human consumption;
and
whether natural or manufactured; and

whether or not incorporated or mixed
with other goods.

In this Division, a reference to economic loss
caused through public awareness of the
contamination of goods includes a reference to
economic loss caused through—

members of the public not purchasing or
using those goods or similar goods; or

steps taken to avoid public alarm or anxiety
or to avoid harm to members of the public.

nodes.heading: Contaminating goods with intent to cause, or being reckless as to whether it would cause, public alarm or economic loss
nodes.text:
A person must not contaminate goods with the
intention of causing, or being reckless as to
whether or not the contamination would cause—
Penalty: Level 5 imprisonment (10 years
maximum) or a level 5 fine
(1200 penalty units maximum) or both.

history.raw: New s. 249 inserted by No. 65/1998 s. 5, amended by No. 66/2005 s. 3(2)(a).
Note to s. 249 inserted by No. 80/2001 s. 7(1).

nodes.text: public alarm or anxiety; or

economic loss through public awareness of
the contamination.

Division 2B of Part 4 of the Sentencing Act 1991 provides for the
making of cost recovery orders in respect of costs incurred by
emergency service agencies in providing an immediate response to
an emergency arising out of the commission of an offence against
this section

nodes.heading: Threatening to contaminate goods with intent to cause, or being reckless as to whether it would cause, public alarm or economic loss

history.raw: New s. 250 inserted by No. 65/1998 s. 5.
Note to s. 250 inserted by No. 80/2001 s. 7(2).

nodes.text:
A person must not make a threat that goods will
be contaminated with the intention of causing, or
being reckless as to whether or not the threat
would cause—
Penalty: Level 5 imprisonment (10 years
maximum) or a level 5 fine
(1200 penalty units maximum) or both.
public alarm or anxiety; or

economic loss through public awareness of
the threat.

For the purposes of this section, a threat may be
made by any conduct, and may be explicit or
implicit and conditional or unconditional.

Division 2B of Part 4 of the Sentencing Act 1991 provides for the
making of cost recovery orders in respect of costs incurred by
emergency service agencies in providing an immediate response to
an emergency arising out of the commission of an offence against
this section.

nodes.heading: Making false statements concerning contamination of goods with intent to cause, or being reckless as to whether it would cause, public alarm or economic loss

history.raw: New s. 251 inserted by No. 65/1998 s. 5.
Note to s. 251 inserted by No. 80/2001 s. 7(3).

nodes.text:
A person must not make a statement that the
person believes to be false—
Penalty: Level 5 imprisonment (10 years
maximum) or a level 5 fine
(1200 penalty units maximum) or both.

with the intention of inducing the person to
whom the statement is made or others to
believe that goods have been contaminated;
and

with the intention of thereby causing, or
being reckless as to whether or not the
statement would cause—
public alarm or anxiety; or

economic loss through public
awareness of the statement.

For the purposes of this section, making a
statement includes conveying information by any
means.

Division 2B of Part 4 of the Sentencing Act 1991 provides for the
making of cost recovery orders in respect of costs incurred by
emergency service agencies in providing an immediate response to
an emergency arising out of the commission of an offence against
this section.

nodes.heading: Territorial nexus for offences
nodes.text:
It is immaterial that the conduct of a person
constituting an offence under this Division
occurred outside Victoria, so long as the person
intended by that conduct to cause, or was reckless
as to whether or not that conduct would cause—

history.raw: New s. 252 inserted by No. 65/1998 s. 5, amended by No. 66/2005 s. 6(a).

nodes.text: public alarm or anxiety in Victoria; or

economic loss in Victoria through public
awareness of the contamination.
